qc = QuantumCircuit(2, 2)
qc.h([0, 1])          # uniform superposition
qc.cz(0, 1)           # oracle: phase-flips |11>
qc.h([0, 1]); qc.x([0, 1]); qc.cz(0, 1); qc.x([0, 1]); qc.h([0, 1])   # diffuser
qc.measure([0, 1], [0, 1])
caption: Searching a 4-item space (|00>,|01>,|10>,|11>) for the single marked item |11>, using one Grover iteration.

steps.label: h([0,1]): uniform superposition
steps.sub: All 4 states at probability 0.25 — nothing favored yet

steps.label: cz(0,1): the oracle
steps.sub: Flips the sign of |11> only — marks it without revealing it or changing any probability

steps.label: The 5-gate diffuser
steps.sub: "Inversion about the mean" — converts that phase flip into a measurement-probability boost

eyebrow: The exact result for N=4, M=1

steps.label: After exactly one full Grover iteration
steps.sub: The resulting state is exactly |11> at probability 1.0 — everything else is 0

steps.label: (π/4)·√(N/M) happens to equal 1 here
steps.sub: For larger N, the optimal count rounds to a nearby integer — close to 1.0, not exact

eyebrow: Why more iterations isn't always better

steps.label: Past the optimal count: it decreases
steps.sub: Two iterations on this same circuit would move backward, not forward

steps.label: qiskit_algorithms.Grover handles it
steps.sub: Builds the matching diffuser and figures out the iteration count automatically

subtitle: The subroutine inside Shor's algorithm and quantum phase estimation.
